title: Checks that apply to every purchase, and the rules every checklist follows

pathGrammar.title: Product title. Free text: a citation must carry a verbatim quote of at most 160 characters.
pathGrammar.description: Product description. Free text: verbatim quote of at most 160 characters. Also scanned for contradictions.
pathGrammar.key_features[]: Any item of key_features. A citation names the index and quotes the item.
pathGrammar.structured_attributes.<key>: Any value in that attribute's list.
pathGrammar.brands[].name: Any brand name on the product.
pathGrammar.category.slug: Channel3 category slug of the product.
pathGrammar.variants.selected[<Name>|<Name>]: Selected label of the variant option whose name matches one of the names (case-insensitive).
pathGrammar.offer.<field>: The offer the agent selected, matched by domain: price.price, availability, condition, domain, dimensions.*
pathGrammar.offers[].<field>: All offers of the product. Used only for contradiction scans, never as backing.

contradictionRule.text: Every test and every askWhen condition is evaluated over every candidate value code finds in the requirement's evidence paths, not only the cited one. All candidates pass: pass. All fail: broken. Mixed: contradictory, which goes into the question showing each value and the field it came from.
examples: RAM 16 GB and 32 GB (two configurations), buyer needs at least 16: pass.
Screen 65 and 55 inches, buyer asked for 65: contradictory.
Resolution '4K ultra HD' and '1920 x 1080': not a contradiction, resolution is read as a maximum (see tv.json).
Synonyms ('4K ultra HD' and '2160p') normalize to one value before comparing.

reasonTypes.broken: Backed by the listing and violated (for example the selected variant is 83 inches and the buyer asked for 65). Goes back to the agent. No question.
reasonTypes.unbacked: The listing does not give the value. Goes into the question.
reasonTypes.contradictory: The listing gives values that lead to different results. Goes into the question.
reasonTypes.never_asked: A requirement the buyer never stated but the request makes relevant (the request mentions the wall, so the TV's mount pattern must fit; it mentions a trip, so the dryer must take 220-240 V), and the listing gives a value the buyer must confirm. Goes into the question. Since 2026-11-10 no requirement applies 'always': every one is stated or triggered by the request.
reasonTypes.payment: An offer or payment check from this file (price, stock, condition, quantity, variant, store, duplicate, amount). Goes back to the agent, except price_unchanged and an unknown condition, which go into the question.

question.polarity: Every line describes the gap and asks whether it is OK. yes = OK, pay as far as this line goes. no = not OK. dont_know = not sure.
question.outcome: Capture only if every line is answered yes. Any no or dont_know: not captured, back to the agent with the reasons.
question.memory: Answers persist for the whole task. yes marks the requirement not needed; no marks it needed (a later product that breaks it goes back to the agent without a question); dont_know leaves it open.
question.overflow: More than 3 lines: no question. Back to the agent with all reasons and the message 'Too many points in this listing cannot be verified; choose a better documented offer.'
question.order: payment, then contradictory, then unbacked, then never_asked.

lines.text: The listing gives two screen sizes: 65 inches (title) and 55 inches (features). Is that OK?
This TV uses the VESA 300 x 300 mm wall-mount pattern (the hole spacing on its back). Does your mount support it?
